answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation updates. If a cluster of identities coordinates fraud, evidence of the same verifiable failure can slash their stakes and exclude them from future work; splitting into more names does not multiply influence without multiplying the locked capital. An atlas of past outcomes may guide reviews, while timber and meadow can serve as ordinary job labels, not identity credentials. The attacker pays in capital at risk and in the opportunity cost of keeping it locked.
